candidates.title: Discovery of the Baltic Sea anomaly on side scan sonar
candidates.place_text: Baltic Sea, between Finland and Sweden
candidates.quote: So, I remember Peter Peter and laughing and oh, Dennis, you know, here is UFO.

link.reason: Both tell of Dennis Asberg's team finding the Millennium-Falcon-shaped object on sonar in the Baltic between Sweden and Finland; this is the finder's own account of that find.
link.difference: Told firsthand by Asberg, who dates it to 19 June 2011, says it showed up on side scan sonar and names Peter Lindberg and Floris.

candidates.title: Going public with the find through Expressen
candidates.quote: So, I talked to a journalist here in Stockholm, Expressen is a big newspaper.

link.reason: Taking the find to the newspaper Expressen is a separate event after the discovery; no story covers it.

candidates.title: Phantom radar contact near the anomaly
candidates.quote: we are alone here. But should be something 150 m from us. Nothing there.

link.reason: A phantom radar contact at the site is one incident within the wider anomaly lore; no story covers it.

candidates.title: ROV, camera and lights fail at the object
candidates.quote: >> Yep. And when we have dive on it, the camera stops working, the light stops working.

link.reason: The ROV, camera and lights failing during dives is a distinct incident at the site; no story covers it.

candidates.title: GPS lost over the object on the Stockholm University ship
candidates.quote: And then we go over the object and Tomas said to me, "Dennis, we have problems with the GPS function."

link.reason: The GPS loss on the Stockholm University ship in June 2025 is a separate, later incident; no story covers it.

candidates.title: Stefan Hogeborn's 2012 dive: dark black surface and near-freezing water
candidates.quote: >> No, Stiafon was one of the divers down there 2012 and he brushed off the sediment of it and it's dark black.

link.reason: Stefan Hogeborn's 2012 dive, where he found a dark black surface and near-freezing water, is one specific dive and not the general anomaly story.

candidates.title: The breathing hole on the object
candidates.quote: >> yeah, dusty. And then you see like it's from this hole this milk is going Uh-huh.

link.reason: The breathing hole with milky outflow is a separate claim about the object, even though it comes from the 2012 dives; #6 is about the surface and the water temperature.

candidates.title: Diver calls it the most important dive of his life
candidates.quote: >> That was probably the most important dive I've ever done in my life. I've done maybe 6,000 dives in my life.

link.reason: This is Hogeborn's own judgement of how important the dive was, not an account of what the dive found, so it is distinct from #6.

candidates.title: Loose stone samples tested in Israel turn out to be basalt
candidates.quote: And basalt, volcanic stones they found.

link.reason: Testing stone samples in Israel and finding basalt is a separate event; the basalt stories in the corpus are about Turkey and are unrelated.

candidates.title: Skeptical Finnish ROV team calls it man-made and like a power line
candidates.quote: This must be man-made. This is constructed."

link.reason: The skeptical Finnish ROV team's 2019 verdict is a separate event; no story covers it.

candidates.title: Thunder and lightning striking the spot
candidates.quote: weather phenomenons like thunder thunder and and lots of things just on the spot.

link.reason: Weather events such as thunder striking the anomaly site are one detail of the site's lore. The nearest story is the Baltic Sea anomaly expedition as a whole, which is broader.

candidates.title: Remote viewers describe the anomaly as a constructed gold energy source
candidates.quote: Oh, that is constructed and it's some of us have it made of gold.

link.reason: A 2025 remote-viewing reading of the Baltic anomaly as a gold energy source. The remote-viewing stories in the corpus are about other targets (the Moon, Tunguska, the CIA program), and the Finnish ROV team's 'man-made' judgment is a different source.

candidates.title: Big meteor over Åland the day after the June trip
candidates.quote: So, it was on the news that the big meteor over Åland and over here.

link.reason: A meteor over Åland reported on the news in June 2025. No story covers it.

candidates.title: NATO warships around the expedition
candidates.quote: >> It's NATO. It was French and German and American and British ships around us.

link.reason: NATO warships around the expedition are one incident during the anomaly dives. The expedition story is broader and does not tell this incident.

candidates.title: Swedish navy ship heads straight for the dive boat
candidates.quote: >> Suddenly we saw in the distance that this must be some [music] kind of navy ship heading directly on us.

link.reason: A Swedish navy ship heading straight for the dive boat is a different incident from the multinational NATO ships in #4. No story covers it.

candidates.title: Denial at the meeting at Swedish military headquarters
candidates.quote: And he just look at me. "No, no, no, no, no. We have not been there." "But you have been filming you. I have filmed you. So, I know you have been there."

link.reason: A denial at a meeting at Swedish military headquarters is a distinct event. No story covers it.

candidates.quote: were home they I got the call from the Swedish let's say it's like FBI in Sweden

link.reason: The security service's call over the Som find is one event inside #7, which also covers the find itself. That makes it narrower, so it cannot be 'same'.

candidates.title: Wrecks carrying liquor, including wine from the 1600s
candidates.quote: We found also one of the oldest wine in the world from 1600. Wow.

link.reason: Liquor wrecks and 1600s wine found around 2005 are an earlier set of finds. No story covers them.

candidates.title: New data show the object separated from the seabed
candidates.quote: It looks like it's separated from the bottom. That's what I can say.

link.reason: June 2025 data showing the object separated from the seabed is one finding about the anomaly. The expedition story is broader.

link.reason: No stored story says the Baltic object was built before the ice age. The remote viewers' gold energy-source story makes a different claim, and Hancock's lost civilization is about other sites.

link.reason: No stored story covers a 1996 sighting of a round craft over a military site near Stockholm.
